name: Portfolio Allocation
rationale: Static allocation rules test whether simple diversification beats single-asset exposure on risk-adjusted terms.
expected_benefit: Lower drawdown and smoother returns through diversification rather than timing.
failure_modes: Static weights can underperform concentrated equity exposure.
Benchmark choice can dominate the interpretation.

canonical_variants.name: Equal-weight two-asset portfolio
canonical_variants.description: Hold two assets at fixed equal weights.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A static two-asset equal-weight portfolio may reduce drawdown versus SPY buy-and-hold while retaining acceptable growth.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative while retaining at least 70% of SPY benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Equity/bond 60/40
canonical_variants.description: Hold a fixed 60% equity and 40% bond allocation.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A simple 60/40 equity-bond portfolio may improve drawdown-adjusted performance versus SPY buy-and-hold.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 25% relative while retaining at least 60% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Three-asset static defensive mix
canonical_variants.description: Hold equities, bonds, and cash-like exposure at fixed weights.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A static defensive multi-asset mix may reduce drawdown enough to justify lower raw return versus SPY.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 30% relative while retaining at least 50% of benchmark CAGR.

suggested_validation: Use portfolio workflow, not single-strategy workflow.
Audit every symbol's data and shared date range.
Compare to both SPY and a matched static benchmark when available.
execution_notes: The portfolio engine supports static weights, but ideas suggest currently emits a generic draft config rather than a portfolio plan.
